summary:
Stopped before planning holding-renamed-and-rebound (migration-tools#r3). Two reasons.
1. The research notes are not there. The research result.json says 'Notes in notes.md (partial until finished)', but .shop/work/i8-model-in-consumers/runs/holding-renamed-and-rebound/1-research/ holds only brief.md, result.json and session.json. Without notes there is no list of broken tests and no detail of plan_holding in scripts/migrate_spec.py to plan from.
2. The accepted scenario does not formulate the changed r3. The only @r3 scenario, '`migrate run` deprecates a @holding scenario as `features deprecate` does', asserts that the result equals what `features deprecate` gives. Under feature-file-tools#r19, `features deprecate` appends ' (deprecated)', changes nothing else and rebinds no test. The changed r3 puts ' (deprecated)' in place of ' (held)' and rebinds each test. The research says this scenario already passes today, so nothing would go red and then green. A scenario for the changed r3 needs to be formulated and accepted, and the old one deprecated and listed under Retires, before this can be planned.
On the researcher's second question: the probe shows 'held one (deprecated)', and that is the current behaviour. The work-item's 'held one (held) (deprecated)' is what `features deprecate` would give a title that ends in ' (held)'.
No plan.md was written.
questions: Research notes are missing: .shop/work/i8-model-in-consumers/runs/holding-renamed-and-rebound/1-research/notes.md does not exist, although the research result says it was written. Re-run research, or recover the notes, so the plan can name the tests that break and what plan_holding does today.

Which governs r3: the accepted scenario or the changed requirement text? Reading A (the scenario as accepted, 'as `features deprecate` does'): a @holding scenario titled 'held one (held)' comes out of migrate as 'held one (held) (deprecated)', and a test that names it keeps the old title and is left unbound, the same as the copy `features deprecate` gives (feature-file-tools#r19). It already passes, so this work-item has nothing to make green. Reading B (r3 as changed): migrate's output is 'held one (deprecated)' with 'Deprecated for:' in place of 'Held for:', and each test that named 'held one (held)' is rebound to the new title and stays bound. This needs a new @r3 scenario formulated and accepted, with the old scenario deprecated and named under the work-item's Retires.
